title: Surviving readout errors and incomplete postselection in monitored quantum circuits
authors: Murtaza Ali Mir, Teemu Ojanen, Ali G. Moghaddam
abstract: We study how readout errors affect dynamics in monitored quantum circuits. Such errors make postselection effectively incomplete, conditioning trajectories on imperfect rather than true records. Focusing on U(1)-symmetric circuits, we find that the charge-sharpening transition survives at a finite error rate, with the sharp phase's vanishing fluctuations replaced by a finite steady-state plateau. The charge fluctuations show a shallow minimum near the ideal transition point as a function of measurement rate, signaling the competition between measurement-induced purification and noise-induced mixing. By decomposing the fluctuations into quantum and classical contributions, we show the minimum marks where incomplete postselection still retains enough trajectory memory to attenuate noise-induced mixing, leaving a detectable signature of the transition even in a noisy setting. Mid-circuit measurements are far harder to mitigate against readout errors than standard end-of-circuit ones, because the errors corrupt the postselection itself; the decomposition therefore offers a minimal mitigation framework and a route to locate the transition directly from experimental data. Our results show that charge sharpening survives readout errors in a quantitative and experimentally accessible way.
summary: This paper analyzes how readout errors degrade the signature of measurement-induced phase transitions in monitored quantum circuits. By decomposing charge fluctuations, the authors show that the transition survives noise, leaving a measurable plateau and a characteristic minimum in the fluctuation spectrum. This provides a vital diagnostic tool for interpreting noisy experimental data from quantum measurement processes.
main_problem: The paper investigates how readout errors and incomplete postselection corrupt the dynamics and observable signatures of measurement-induced phase transitions (MIPTs) in monitored quantum circuits.
main_result: The charge-sharpening transition survives finite readout error rates, manifesting as a finite steady-state plateau rather than vanishing fluctuations, and a shallow minimum in fluctuations signals the competition between purification and noise.
method: The analysis uses a quantum-trajectory framework, decomposing the charge fluctuations into quantum and classical contributions to isolate the effects of noise and memory.
model_or_system: The study focuses on U(1)-symmetric monitored quantum circuits, modeling the dynamics under the influence of imperfect measurement records (readout errors).
key_observables: Charge fluctuations ($\delta^2Q$), normalized charge fluctuation $F(t)$, and the hybrid probe $\Delta F = F - F_{	ext{approx}}^{cl}$.
important_parameters: Readout error rate ($\eta$), measurement rate ($p_m$), and the ideal transition point ($p_\#$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that postselection is based on imperfectly recorded outcomes, leading to incomplete postselection.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the suppression of fluctuations in the ideal case versus the residual plateau at finite error rates, and show the three-regime structure of fluctuations versus measurement rate.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by calculating the noisy ensemble density matrix $ho_{	ilde{m}}$, separating the variance into quantum and classical parts, and then analyzing how the resulting fluctuations behave across different measurement rate regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a quantitative and experimentally accessible method to detect fundamental quantum phase transitions in noisy, realistic quantum hardware settings, which is crucial for experimental quantum information science.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of a U(1)-symmetric monitored circuit. Two-qubit gates (purple blocks) are drawn from the Haar measure restricted to U(1) charge-conserving unitaries. After each layer of gates, every qubit is measured independently with probability pm. Correctly recorded measurement out- comes are shown in blue, and outcomes affected by assign- ment (readout) errors are shown in red.

FIG. 2. Charge-fluctuation dynamics in the presence of readout error. (a) Heat map of the normalized charge fluctuation F(t) = δ2Q(t)/(L/4) as a function of time t and measurement rate pm, at fixed assignment error rate η = 5%. (b),(c),(d) Time evolution of F(t) for pm = 0.04, 0.1, 0.8, respectively. Ideal measurements suppress charge fluctuations efficiently, while finite assignment error leaves a residual long-time fluctuation. Nonetheless, the qualitative distinction between the two monitoring regimes persists in the presence of noise: F(t) decays slowly at low pm (b) and around the charge sharpening transition pm ∼0.1 (c), while it saturates rapidly to a finite plateau at high pm (d)....

FIG. 3. Steady-state charge fluctuations in the presence of readout error. (a) Heat map of the normalized charge fluctuation F(T) at long time T = 8L, as a function of measurement rate pm (near the sharpening transition, pm ∼0.1) and error rate η. (b) Measurement-rate dependence of the fluctuations for various error strengths. (c) Growth of the fluctuations with error strength for various values of pm. Panels (a)–(c) are all for L = 12; panel (d) shows that other system sizes exhibit the same pattern, with only a slight decrease in the depth of the minimum with increasing size.

FIG. 4. Noise-induced mixing and its associated extra fluctuations. (a) The noise-induced (classical) contribution Fcl as a function of measurement rate pm, for different er- ror rates (solid lines); the reason for calling this term clas- sical is explained in the main text. Dashed lines show the corresponding prediction assuming uncorrelated errors, gov- erned by the Bernoulli noise-variance form (denoted Fapprox cl in the main text). (b) The residual fluctuation after sub- tracting the uncorrelated classical estimate from the total, ∆F = F −F approx cl . All the results are obtained for length L = 12.
